angle: Precomputed and learned light-transport OPERATORS (PRT and all-frequency/glossy variants, direct-to-indirect and wavelet/meshless transport matrices, modular reduced operators with interfaces, per-object fields for rigid dynamic scenes, radiance regression, neural PRT, neural radiosity and dynamic successors, neural GI over scene parameters, generalizing feed-forward transport predictors, operator/Green's-function learning) and what each keeps valid when geometry is rigidly edited. Method: web search plus reading of primary pages where reachable; 9 of 30 entries were read from the primary paper text (MRT, Shadow Fields, Neural Radiosity, Raghavan et al. 2023, Active Exploration, TransGI, OSF, RenderFormer, Xu et al. 2025); the rest are abstract/project-page level, with mechanism details beyond the abstract flagged as recalled.

entries.work: Sloan, Kautz, Snyder — Precomputed Radiance Transfer for Real-Time Rendering in Dynamic, Low-Frequency Lighting Environments
entries.mechanism: Per-vertex linear transfer (vectors for diffuse, matrices for glossy) maps distant low-frequency lighting in spherical harmonics to exit radiance, with self-shadowing and self-interreflection baked in. 'Neighborhood transfer' stores the same kind of operator on a volume around a rigid object so it can cast soft shadows, glossy reflections and caustics onto arbitrary receivers.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-object SH transfer vectors/matrices (self-transfer) and a sampled transfer volume around the object (neighborhood transfer); nothing learned.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Self-transfer of a rigid object survives rigid motion of that object (lighting is rotated into its frame). Neighborhood transfer survives motion of the receiver relative to one object. Anything involving two or more mutually influencing objects, or deformation, is invalidated and needs a new precompute (recalled: receivers do not feed back onto the sender).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Excluded by construction: lighting and transfer are band-limited to low SH orders, so glossy response is low-frequency only.
entries.cost_claims: Real-time rendering after an offline per-object simulation; no path-tracing comparison at matched quality in the sources I read.
entries.limitation: Low-frequency, distant lighting; operator tied to a fixed object; multi-object coupling not representable.
entries.relevance: Origin of the 'source-independent linear operator applied to an encoding of incident light' idea, and of attaching the operator to an object's own frame so rigid motion is free. Shows the price paid from the start: rigid-motion validity was obtained together with a band limit.

entries.work: Ng, Ramamoorthi, Hanrahan — Triple Product Wavelet Integrals for All-Frequency Relighting
entries.mechanism: Shading is the integral of a product of three functions (lighting, visibility, BRDF), each projected to Haar wavelets; the paper analyses triple-product integrals and gives linear/sublinear-time algorithms for Haar, so lighting and view can both change at all frequencies.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-vertex visibility in a wavelet basis and BRDF slices in the same basis; the factors are kept separate rather than baked into one transfer matrix.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: BRDF and lighting factors are geometry-independent; the per-vertex visibility factor is scene-configuration-specific and must be recomputed after any edit (recalled: static geometry only).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Sharp shadows and sharp BRDF lobes for DIRECT lighting only; interreflection is not part of the triple product.
entries.cost_claims: All-frequency lighting up to 6x256x256 cubemaps, changing materials and viewpoint 'in a few seconds' per frame (as summarised from the abstract).
entries.limitation: Direct lighting, static geometry, per-vertex storage; sparsity is obtained by nonlinear coefficient selection that depends on the particular configuration.
entries.relevance: Shows that all-frequency directional relations were made tractable by sparse selection in a localized basis, not by low rank, and by factorising the operator into geometry-independent and geometry-dependent parts — the geometry-dependent part (visibility) is exactly what an edit invalidates.

entries.work: Liu, Sloan, Shum, Snyder — All-Frequency Precomputed Radiance Transfer for Glossy Objects (concurrent: Wang, Tran, Luebke — All-Frequency Relighting of Non-Diffuse Objects using Separable BRDF Approximation)
entries.mechanism: Glossy BRDFs are factorised into view-dependent and light-dependent parts (about 10 terms); per-vertex transfer matrices from a 6x32x32 lighting cube map to these factors are compressed with Haar wavelets over 24 lighting segments plus clustered PCA.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-vertex transfer matrices (lighting basis -> BRDF light-factor coefficients), wavelet + CPCA compressed.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Only a rigid transform of the whole object relative to distant lighting; any relative motion of parts invalidates the matrices.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: All-frequency shadows on glossy receivers under distant light. Whether interreflection is included in the transfer is not confirmed from what I read; no sender-side sharp lobe is resolved in any case because the output side is a 10-term separable BRDF.
entries.cost_claims: 1-5 Hz on models up to 50,000 vertices with 2-3 orders of magnitude more lighting coefficients than SH PRT.
entries.limitation: Static geometry, distant lighting, low-term separable BRDF limits specular sharpness on the view side.
entries.relevance: The glossy all-frequency transfer matrix is the classical analogue of a (patch x direction) transport table; its size forced both a separable angular factorisation and scene-specific compression.

entries.work: Zhou, Hu, Lin, Guo, Shum — Precomputed Shadow Fields for Dynamic Scenes
entries.mechanism: Each rigid entity carries a field sampled on concentric spheres around it: a source radiance field (SRF) for lights and an object occlusion field (OOF) for occluders, each sample being a cube map in the entity's local frame. At run time the incident radiance at a receiver is assembled by rotating and multiplying the fields of the entities between receiver and light (SH products for low frequency, wavelet products for all-frequency).
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-entity SRF/OOF on shells (e.g. 6x16x16 directions for low frequency; 32 spheres of 6x32x32 for all-frequency), SH or wavelet compressed (about 268 non-zero wavelet coefficients per sample); per-vertex self-visibility. Nothing learned.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Everything: fields are independent of scene configuration, so arbitrary rigid motion of any object or local light needs no recomputation, and instances share one field. Deformation is not covered.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Excluded. The paper states it handles only direct lighting and lists interreflection as future work. All-frequency refers to shadows.
entries.cost_claims: Low-frequency: 12-30 fps at 15-50 MB; all-frequency: 0.1 fps (Spaceships, 280 MB) to 7-16 fps (relighting, 500 MB); precompute under two hours for all-frequency fields.
entries.limitation: Direct lighting only; sampling density chosen by experiment with no theory; all-frequency fields are large and slow; fields cannot be evaluated inside another object's bounding region without care.
entries.relevance: The clearest demonstration that full rigid-edit validity is obtainable by making each object own a field in its own frame and composing at run time — and that doing so at all frequencies already cost two orders of magnitude in speed for visibility alone, before any interreflection.

entries.work: Pan et al. — Precomputed Radiance Transfer Field for Rendering Interreflections in Dynamic Scenes (related: Iwasaki, Dobashi, Yoshimoto, Nishita — PRT for Dynamic Scenes Taking into Account Light Interreflection, EGSR 2007; Mei, Shi, Wu — Spherical Radiance Transport Maps, CGF 2004)
entries.mechanism: A radiance transfer field records, for an object, the radiance it sends to sample points in its surrounding space as a linear function of the radiance incident on the object. Because this is independent of the rest of the scene it plugs into the shadow-field framework and adds inter-object interreflection for rigidly moving objects.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-object linear operator: incident lighting coefficients on the object -> radiance field around it, compressed with clustered PCA.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The per-object operator is valid under any rigid rearrangement; composition is done at run time. Deformation invalidates it.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Diffuse and glossy senders are supported, but only under low-frequency lighting (SH); sharp sender lobes are band-limited away.
entries.cost_claims: Abstract claims negligible extra cost over shadow fields for adding interreflection; data highly compressible by CPCA. No numbers read.
entries.limitation: Low-frequency restriction; incident light on the sender is summarised by a few coefficients (recalled: effectively one incident-lighting estimate per object), so near-field and sharp directional relations between sender and receiver are lost.
entries.relevance: The nearest classical precedent to a source-independent, per-object, composable interreflection operator that survives rigid edits. Its validity under edits was bought with exactly the restriction (low angular frequency of the sender response) that the light -> sharp reflector -> diffuse family violates.

entries.work: Hašan, Pellacini, Bala — Direct-to-Indirect Transfer for Cinematic Relighting
entries.mechanism: For a fixed view, multi-bounce indirect light at view samples is a linear transform of direct light on a large cloud of gather samples. The huge matrix is precomputed hierarchically and stored sparsely in a wavelet basis imposed on the unstructured gather cloud.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A sparse wavelet-space direct-to-indirect matrix (gather samples -> view samples), source-independent: any direct lighting, computed by any shader, is the input.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing; fixed geometry and fixed camera. Any edit requires recomputing the matrix (precompute under three hours on one processor).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Multi-bounce diffuse indirect; recalled: glossy allowed at the final view sample but gather samples are treated as diffuse senders, so sharp sender lobes are not carried.
entries.cost_claims: 10-20 fps on scenes with over 2 million polygons after an under-3-hour precompute.
entries.limitation: Fixed view and geometry; sender side is direction-collapsed.
entries.relevance: The canonical 'direct light encoding in, indirect out' source-independent operator. It is the explicit matrix that a geometry-conditioned generator would have to emit, and it shows that its sparsity structure (wavelet) is specific to one geometry.

entries.work: Kontkanen, Turquin, Holzschuch, Sillion — Wavelet Radiance Transport for Interactive Indirect Lighting
entries.mechanism: Radiance is represented in a 4D (space x direction) wavelet basis; a Global Transport Operator that propagates radiance through the scene (all bounces) is precomputed hierarchically; at run time direct lighting is projected onto the basis and multiplied by the operator.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A 4D-wavelet global transport operator (direct radiance -> converged indirect radiance) for diffuse and glossy materials.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing; the abstract states static scenes only. The operator is a property of one configuration.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Glossy materials are included in the operator through the directional dimensions of the wavelet basis; how sharp a lobe was actually demonstrated is not verified here.
entries.cost_claims: Interactive manipulation of lighting; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Static geometry; hierarchical 4D wavelets were demonstrated on simple, smooth surface parameterisations (as noted by the later meshless work).
entries.relevance: A direct classical counterpart of a (patch x outgoing-direction) <- (patch x incident-direction) transport table with glossy senders. It establishes that such an operator is representable in a hierarchical directional basis for one fixed scene, and says nothing about reuse across configurations.

entries.work: Lehtinen, Zwicker, Turquin, Kontkanen, Durand, Sillion, Aila — A Meshless Hierarchical Representation for Light Transport
entries.mechanism: A hierarchical basis built from scattered-data approximation over points, decoupled from the surface representation, is used for a precomputed direct-to-indirect transport algorithm on complex geometry.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Direct-to-indirect transport operator expressed in the meshless hierarchical basis.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The basis construction is geometry-agnostic, but the operator is precomputed per scene; an edit requires recomputation (recalled: static scenes).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not verified; recalled as primarily diffuse indirect with smooth basis functions, which would not resolve sharp sender lobes.
entries.cost_claims: Abstract claims a large increase in the scene complexity PRT can handle and shorter precomputation than per-vertex bases; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Per-scene operator; smooth spatial basis.
entries.relevance: Shows the operator basis can be freed from meshing/parameterisation (relevant to patch choice), while the operator entries themselves remain tied to one configuration.

entries.work: Loos, Antani, Mitchell, Nowrouzezahrai, Jarosz, Sloan — Modular Radiance Transfer
entries.mechanism: A small dictionary of simple shapes (cubes with missing faces, cylinders) each carries reduced direct-to-indirect operators. A low-rank 'light prior' (SVD of direct lighting from implicit lights, kd = 64, kself = 32) defines the input subspace; light leaving a shape through an open face is carried as a reduced interface lightfield (raw 12^2 spatial x 24^2 directional, then SVD) and propagated to neighbouring shapes by precomputed interface-to-interface operators. Shapes are instanced, warped and connected at run time.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per dictionary shape, once and scene-independently: light prior bases, shape self-transfer, surface-to-interface, interface-to-interface and interface-to-surface operators, plus a volumetric operator for lighting dynamic characters. All dense low-rank matrices.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: All operators: scenes are assembled and re-assembled from the dictionary without scene-dependent precomputation. Actual scene geometry is only approximated by warped proxies; dynamic objects receive light from a volume but do not cast indirect shadows (the paper states indirect shadows are ignored).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Excluded. The paper targets diffuse, coarse-scale indirect light and states that extending the approach to high-frequency glossy transport while keeping its benefits is a challenging open problem.
entries.cost_claims: Over 475 FPS on high-end GPUs and over 45 FPS on mobile for a 19-block scene; 2.1 ms versus 'many hours' for ground truth (not at matched quality).
entries.limitation: Stated in the paper: lighting conditions outside the low-rank prior cannot be captured (e.g. a light too close to a wall); results are 'plausible' rather than accurate; a single proxy degenerates to an 'intelligent ambient term'.
entries.relevance: The strongest precedent for reusable reduced operators with explicit interfaces that stay valid under re-arrangement. It documents the generic behaviour of reduced operators: what is outside the prior's span is replaced by a smooth, geometrically unspecific response.

entries.work: Drettakis, Sillion — Interactive Update of Global Illumination Using a Line-Space Hierarchy
entries.mechanism: Hierarchical-radiosity links between clusters/surfaces are augmented with shafts (the set of lines through both linked elements). When an object moves, traversing this implicit line-space hierarchy identifies exactly the links whose transport changed and re-solves only those, with the traversal depth bounded by the frame-time budget.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: The link structure (the discretised transport operator) and its shafts; nothing learned.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: All links whose shaft is not intersected by the swept moved object stay valid untouched; intersected links are recomputed, and subdivision that is no longer needed is cleaned up.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Excluded: diffuse hierarchical radiosity with clustering.
entries.cost_claims: Interactive updates (2-3 frames per second) after object motion for scenes of several thousand polygons on 1997 hardware.
entries.limitation: Diffuse only; update cost grows with the number of affected links, which grows with the directional resolution of the operator.
entries.relevance: Establishes that the subset of operator entries invalidated by a rigid move is geometrically identifiable without re-solving everything — the explicit-operator answer to 'what stays valid under an edit'. It was never carried to directional (glossy) links in the work I found.

entries.work: Xu, Cao, Ma, Dong, Wang, Hu — A Practical Algorithm for Rendering Interreflections with All-Frequency BRDFs
entries.mechanism: With BRDFs represented as spherical Gaussians, one-bounce interreflection from a reflector triangle to a shading point is evaluated by an analytic formula plus a piecewise-linear approximation; a hierarchical integration over triangles with bounded error handles complex scenes on the GPU.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Essentially nothing scene-specific (SG fits of the BRDFs; a triangle hierarchy); the transport is evaluated analytically per frame.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Everything, since no transport is cached (recalled: dynamic scenes, lights and BRDFs supported).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: This is its target: the integration is sender-centred (per reflector triangle, with the sender's SG lobe in closed form) so highly glossy senders, where VPL methods fail, are handled; one bounce only.
entries.cost_claims: Interactive GPU rates reported; no figure read.
entries.limitation: One-bounce interreflection; visibility for the indirect bounce is approximate (recalled); cost scales with reflector triangles.
entries.relevance: A non-learned, edit-proof evaluation of exactly the light -> glossy sender -> receiver family, obtained by integrating over the sender with its lobe known analytically rather than gathering from the receiver. It marks what a reusable operator has to compete against for that family.

entries.work: Ren, Wang, Gong, Lin, Tong, Guo — Global Illumination with Radiance Regression Functions
entries.mechanism: A small feed-forward network regresses indirect radiance at a surface point from its position, view direction and the (point) light's parameters, augmented with local attributes; the input space is partitioned and one small network is fitted per region.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-scene networks trained on offline path-traced shading samples.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing in the transport itself: geometry is baked into the weights; only light position and view are free inputs (the abstract covers dynamic local lights; moving geometry is not addressed).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Claims real-time 'multiple-bounce high-frequency glossy interreflections' and changing caustics for the trained scene; not linear in the source (one point light as input).
entries.cost_claims: Real-time evaluation after offline precomputation; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Scene-specific and source-specific (parameterised light), no geometric generalisation.
entries.relevance: Earliest learned transport response with sharp glossy indirect effects; shows such effects are learnable when geometry is fixed and the source is a low-dimensional parameter — the opposite corner from a geometry-conditioned, source-independent operator.

entries.work: Rainer, Bousseau, Ritschel, Drettakis — Neural Precomputed Radiance Transfer (see also Lyu et al., Neural Radiance Transfer Fields, ECCV 2022, arXiv 2207.13607)
entries.mechanism: Small per-scene networks take per-pixel G-buffer attributes and an encoded environment light and output radiance. The PRT-inspired variant first maps G-buffer inputs to a transport code, then combines it with the light code; further variants factor out albedo and split diffuse/specular tracks.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-scene network weights (transport code predictor + light encoder), trained on rendered data.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing; one fixed scene. Lighting (distant) and view vary.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: View-dependent effects via a specular track; a later paper (Raghavan et al. 2023) characterises it as suited to largely diffuse scenes with less accurate indirect view-dependent effects.
entries.cost_claims: Over 30 FPS neural renderers at a fixed parameter budget.
entries.limitation: Fixed scene, distant lighting, transport code is not constrained to be linear or non-negative.
entries.relevance: Shows that architecture mirroring the operator structure (transport code separate from light code) matters more than size; but the 'transport code' is still memorised per scene.

entries.work: Raghavan, Xiao, Lin, Sun, Bi, Xu, Li, Ramamoorthi — Neural Free-Viewpoint Relighting for Glossy Indirect Illumination
entries.mechanism: The indirect light-transport function T_k(x, w_o) is represented in the Haar wavelet basis over a cube map: outgoing radiance is a dot product of the lighting's largest (typically 64) wavelet coefficients with transport coefficients predicted by a small MLP from a tensor-factorised feature field indexed by position and wavelet index, plus reflected direction, normal and BRDF parameters.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per scene: about 4,000 path-traced training images; hash-grid spatial features, a 6x64x64 wavelet feature grid and an MLP (about 113 MB). Linear in lighting by construction.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing; the paper restricts itself to static scenes and explicitly excludes dynamic objects. Retraining is required after any edit.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Its focus: glossy indirect reflections and view-dependent caustics with changing view, kept sharp by staying in an orthonormal localized basis. Reported failure: a mirror of roughness 0.05 (the reflected painting is not reconstructed); only 64 wavelets are used and selection changes can flicker.
entries.cost_claims: 1-3 hours precomputation plus about 16 hours training on an RTX 3090 Ti; 24 FPS at 512x512 and 13 FPS at 800x600 on an RTX 4090; frame time independent of geometric complexity.
entries.limitation: Static geometry, distant lighting, many hours per scene, residual blur at near-mirror roughness.
entries.relevance: The current reference point for a learned, source-independent linear transport operator that keeps glossy indirect detail — and it does so only per fixed scene, with a localized (not low-rank) lighting basis, and still degrades at the near-mirror end.

entries.work: Hadadan, Chen, Zwicker — Neural Radiosity
entries.mechanism: A network representing the full 4D radiance field of one scene is optimised to minimise the norm of the rendering-equation residual, with the same network on both sides (self-training); views are rendered afterwards with one query per sample (left-hand side) or one extra bounce (right-hand side).
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-scene network weights and learnable multi-resolution features; source and geometry are both baked in.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing formally; the paper shows fine-tuning from a related configuration (a few steps between two poses of one model) instead of retraining from scratch, and names dynamic scenes as future work.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Perfect mirrors are never stored: rays are traced through specular bounces until a non-specular surface and the network is queried there. Glossy reflections depend on capacity and on feeding local surface properties; narrower networks struggle with reflections.
entries.cost_claims: Training 22 minutes (Cornell box) to about 7 hours (bedroom) on an RTX 2080; equal-time LHS rendering beats 16-spp path tracing in one example; the authors state training is not competitive with state-of-the-art Monte Carlo.
entries.limitation: A solver, not a reusable operator: the solution is for one scene and one lighting.
entries.relevance: Shows the standard division of labour for sharp relations in learned GI: trace specular chains explicitly and query the learned quantity only at rough vertices. It also is the nearest thing to a 'neural solver' of the rendering equation; no source-independence, no transfer.

entries.work: Su, Dong, Ren, Jin, Chen, Wang, Li — Dynamic Neural Radiosity with Multi-grid Decomposition
entries.mechanism: Neural radiosity extended to variable scenes: an explicit scene-parameter vector v conditions the radiance field, which is factorised into 3D grids, 2D feature planes over (space, variable) pairs and small MLPs.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-scene feature grids and MLPs trained by the residual objective over the predefined ranges of the scene variables.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Edits that correspond to a point inside the trained variable ranges are served without retraining; any new degree of freedom or range requires retraining (inferred from the formulation; the project page does not state out-of-range behaviour).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not stated on the page read; inherits the neural-radiosity treatment.
entries.cost_claims: Abstract claims reduced training and inference cost versus prior state of the art at practical run-time; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Per scene; variables must be enumerated in advance; memory grows with the number of variables.
entries.relevance: Represents the 'rigid pose as an input coordinate of a per-scene radiance solution' route to edit validity: validity is interpolation inside a trained hypercube, not transfer of an operator to an unseen configuration.

entries.work: Ren, Jin, Pang, Chen, Wang, Li — Neural Cone Radiosity for Interactive Global Illumination with Glossy Materials (2025); Ren et al. — OctaOctree Neural Radiosity for Real-time Glossy Material Rendering (2026)
entries.mechanism: Both address the failure of position-encoded radiance caches on narrow lobes. Cone radiosity encodes a reflectance-aware ray cone with a pre-filtered multi-resolution hash grid approximating the BSDF lobe. OctaOctree stores outgoing radiance in an adaptive octree whose nodes hold octahedral directional maps, with coarser spatial levels carrying higher angular resolution.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per-scene learned encodings and networks in the neural-radiosity framework.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not stated in either abstract; both are in the per-scene neural-radiosity line, so an edit implies re-solving.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Their stated purpose: cached radiance that remains accurate when queried through sharp lobes, by trading spatial for angular resolution (OctaOctree) or by lobe-matched pre-filtering (cone encoding); claimed range from mirror-like to matte.
entries.cost_claims: Real-time, single network query at the primary hit (OctaOctree); no numbers in the abstracts.
entries.limitation: Abstract-level evidence only; per-scene; no statement on dynamic geometry.
entries.relevance: Direct evidence that 'a lookup at a near-mirror receiver exposes localised errors' is a recognised problem of cached outgoing-radiance tables, and that the published responses are angular-resolution-adaptive storage at fixed geometry.

entries.work: Diolatzis, Philip, Drettakis — Active Exploration for Neural Global Illumination of Variable Scenes
entries.mechanism: A per-scene MLP generator (8 layers x 512) maps per-pixel G-buffers plus an explicit scene-parameter vector (object translation/rotation, light position/intensity, material parameters, on/off events) to radiance; training samples are chosen by an MCMC 'active exploration' over the parameter space interleaved with on-the-fly path tracing and sample reuse.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: One network per variable scene, trained on path-traced patches over a normalised hypercube of 6-11 (up to 128) variables.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Rigid edits that are among the declared variables and inside the trained range; the paper reports no test outside the range. New edits require retraining.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: All path types, including mirror reflections and caustics, are learned from data; the authors note high-frequency specular effects may not be reproduced exactly and suggest tracing specular bounces during buffer generation to reduce what the network must infer.
entries.cost_claims: Training 5-18 hours on one RTX 6000; inference 4-6 fps at 900x900 (unoptimised).
entries.limitation: Stated: memory grows with the tiled variable vector; the 128-variable scene has missing shadows and highlights; scene-specific.
entries.relevance: Shows that sharp transport under rigid pose changes can be learned when the edit space is declared in advance and sampled adaptively, at a cost of hours per scene; it is conditioning on a pose vector, not on geometry, so it does not transfer.

entries.work: Granskog, Rousselle, Papas, Novák — Compositional Neural Scene Representations for Shading Inference (2020); Granskog, Schnabel, Rousselle, Novák — Neural Scene Graph Rendering (2021)
entries.mechanism: Learned scene representations are partitioned into lighting, material and geometry components that can be recombined across scenes (2020); in the 2021 work geometry and material are learned vectors at scene-graph leaves, transformations (translation, bending, hue shift) are neural modules at inner nodes, and a streaming neural renderer draws a variable number of objects.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Encoders/decoders and per-asset latent vectors trained across many scenes.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The learned modules are reused when objects are re-arranged via scene-graph transforms; fidelity is that of a learned image generator, with no transport guarantees.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not a stated capability in the abstracts read; these are image-space generators evaluated on comparatively simple shading.
entries.cost_claims: None read.
entries.limitation: No linearity in the source, no physical constraints; inter-object transport is whatever the generator infers.
entries.relevance: Precedent for modular learned components that survive re-arrangement without retraining, obtained by structure (partitioning / scene graph) rather than by a physical operator.

entries.work: Zheng, Huo, Mo, Zhong, Wu, Hua, Wang, Bao — NeLT: Object-Oriented Neural Light Transfer
entries.mechanism: Global illumination is decomposed into per-object neural light-transfer functions describing the light exchange between an object and its surroundings; the per-object functions are composed explicitly so objects can be transformed under dynamic lights.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A neural transfer function per object (details of inputs and lighting encoding not read from the primary source).
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: According to the abstract and secondary summaries, per-object functions are reused under object transformation; deformation is named as missing. Not verified in the paper text.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not verified. The abstract compares quality to a real-time denoiser, which suggests plausible rather than reference-level transport.
entries.cost_claims: Interactive global illumination for dynamic scenes; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Primary text not accessible to me; rigid-only; quality target is 'close to a real-time denoiser'.
entries.relevance: A learned counterpart of radiance-transfer fields: object-owned, composable, rigid-edit-tolerant transfer. Among the closest learned precedents in intent; its angular fidelity is the open question.

entries.work: Deng, Han, Fang — TransGI: Real-Time Dynamic Global Illumination With Object-Centric Neural Transfer Model
entries.mechanism: Per-vertex latent vectors (7 values) plus an MLP decoder output SH transfer coefficients (4th-degree, 75 values) as a function of outgoing direction, normal and albedo; shading is the dot product with SH lighting from an 8x8x8 grid of local light probes that are re-generated every frame with a neighbour 'radiance-sharing' scheme.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Per scene: vertex latents per object and a decoder shared across the scene (object-specific decoders are possible but costly), trained on about 41 M surface samples (about 30 minutes sampling, about 2 hours training). The transfer is linear in lighting.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The transfer features travel with the vertices, so the paper claims rigid transforms work without retraining; the evidence is one desk translation and one sofa shift, rotation is not separately evaluated. Inter-object light is not in the transfer; it is re-supplied by the probes each frame.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Excluded in effect: a fixed 25-function SH basis per channel; the paper states specular responses need an extra per-pixel traced ray, largest errors are on glossy surfaces, and sparse probes miss bright interreflection between two glossy objects.
entries.cost_claims: 6.7 ms per frame versus 1.7 ms for DDGI on an RTX 5000; better RMSE/SSIM than DDGI; network 799 KB, vertex features up to 42 MB.
entries.limitation: Low angular frequency; inter-object interreflection limited by probe density; preprint with thin dynamic evaluation.
entries.relevance: A recent learned system that is explicit about the same split: object-owned linear transfer survives rigid motion, while everything between objects is delegated to a per-frame low-frequency lighting state — and sharp inter-object relations are what is lost.

entries.work: Yu, Guo, Fathi, Chang, Chan, Gao, Funkhouser, Wu — Learning Object-Centric Neural Scattering Functions for Free-Viewpoint Relighting and Scene Composition
entries.mechanism: Each object has a network mapping (position, distant light direction, outgoing direction) to a cumulative radiance-transfer value and density, i.e. the object's response to an unobstructed distant light. Scenes are composed by volume-rendering shadow rays through other objects' densities and Monte Carlo sampling one indirect bounce.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: One neural scattering function per object, learned from about 500 images per object.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Per-object functions are reused in new arrangements without retraining; inter-object shadows and one bounce are recomputed by ray marching at render time.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not modelled: the paper states the unobstructed-distant-light assumption biases inter-reflection estimates especially for shiny objects, omits transmitted light and caustics, and computes one indirect bounce only.
entries.cost_claims: 0.27 FPS for the base model, 16 FPS with a distilled KiloOSF variant on synthetic opaque objects.
entries.limitation: Distant-light response is not the near-field response; composition is approximate and stated as not guaranteed physically correct.
entries.relevance: Shows what goes wrong when a per-object source-independent response is defined for distant illumination and then reused in near-field multi-object configurations: near-field, sharp inter-object transport is precisely the part that is biased.

entries.work: Ren, Huo, et al. — LightFormer: Light-Oriented Global Neural Rendering in Dynamic Scene
entries.mechanism: Instead of encoding the scene, each light generates virtual point lights that are encoded, with screen-space cues such as visibility, into a neural light representation; a pixel-light attention step gathers the light representations per shading point and a small decoder predicts radiance.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Networks trained across data (light encoder, attention, decoder); VPLs and screen-space cues are regenerated per frame.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Learned weights are intended to be reused under dynamic lights, materials, cameras and animated objects, since geometry enters only through per-frame VPLs and G-buffers.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not stated on the page read; VPL-based formulations classically handle diffuse to moderately glossy transport and fail on sharp glossy senders (as noted in Xu et al. 2014).
entries.cost_claims: Real-time; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Screen-space cues; 'reasonable and realistic' rather than reference-level; generalisation claim not quantified on the page.
entries.relevance: Example of obtaining edit tolerance by conditioning a learned gatherer on per-frame traced samples (here VPLs) rather than on a memorised scene — structurally similar to feeding stratified visibility rays to a generator, and with the same receiver-side sampling of sender detail.

entries.work: Zeng, Dong, Peers, Wu, Tong — RenderFormer: Transformer-based Neural Rendering of Triangle Meshes with Global Illumination (follow-up: Du et al., RenderFormer++, arXiv 2606.30380, abstract only)
entries.mechanism: A sequence of triangle tokens (geometry + GGX reflectance + emission) is processed by a view-independent transformer stage modelling triangle-to-triangle light transport, then a view-dependent stage turns ray-bundle tokens into pixels, with no per-scene training.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Transformer weights trained once on the order of millions of synthetic scenes (Objaverse objects in template rooms, Cycles 4,096-spp targets; about 8 days on 8 A100s — exact counts uncertain).
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The weights: any edit is a new token sequence and a new forward pass; the view-independent stage can be reused across views of a static scene. It is not rotation-invariant (mitigated by augmentation).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Shows diffuse and specular interreflection and glossy reflections, but the paper reports that on average about three specular bounces are modelled correctly and higher orders are dropped; larger triangles degrade reflections.
entries.cost_claims: 0.06-0.10 s per 512x512 frame on an A100 versus 2.7-4.7 s (Cycles, 4,096 adaptive spp + denoise) or 7.8-12 s (4,096 spp); not an equal-quality comparison.
entries.limitation: Stated: trained up to 4,096 triangles (quadratic attention), detail lost at 45k; only 1-8 white diffuse lights outside the scene (workaround: render lights separately and sum); single material model without textures; camera outside the scene. The follow-up adds rendering-equation-inspired attention biases, a transport-consistency loss and object-level tokens (abstract only).
entries.relevance: The most developed learned, geometry-conditioned transport model that transfers to unseen configurations without retraining. It is neither linear in the source nor source-independent (superposition is a workaround), it is not constrained to be non-negative or passive, and its documented weak points are higher-order specular chains and scale.

entries.work: Xu, Varma T, Wang, Li, Wu, Wronski, Ramamoorthi, Salvi — A Generalizable Light Transport 3D Embedding for Global Illumination
entries.mechanism: A scene is a point cloud (about 20k points with position, normal, albedo, emissivity; lights are points too). A PointTransformerV3 'light transport encoder' produces latent codes; a query decoder cross-attends to about 32 nearest codes to predict irradiance (or, for glossy, an incident radiance field over 1,024 directions). No rasterised or path-traced cues are input.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Encoder/decoder weights trained across a large indoor dataset (about 5 days on four A10s; dataset about 250 CPU/GPU-days). The paper motivates the design by the transport-matrix view and an attention/matrix-vector analogy but states this is conceptual, and does not claim linearity in lighting.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The weights: moving a sofa, moving an area light or changing floor albedo are shown qualitatively without retraining; the encoder is re-run.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Diffuse irradiance is the main result. Glossy is described as preliminary (conductors at GGX roughness 0.1, fine-tuned encoder). Listed failures include light leaks and missed intricate indirect highlights.
entries.cost_claims: Encoder 208 ms (amortised, view-independent) plus 368 ms decoding for 512x512; compared with 64-spp path tracing; the authors state it is not yet real-time and not a drop-in replacement for path tracing.
entries.limitation: Stated: distribution dependence (indoor), each training scene had a fixed light configuration, colour shifts, light leaks, no quantitative edit evaluation.
entries.relevance: The closest published statement of the goal 'learn a transport embedding conditioned on geometry that is reused across scenes instead of precomputing per scene', by authors from the PRT lineage. It uses no visibility rays, is diffuse-first, and reports sharp indirect highlights as a failure mode.

entries.work: Hermosilla, Maisch, Ritschel, Ropinski — Deep-learning the Latent Space of Light Transport
entries.mechanism: A 3D point-cloud network encodes geometry, material and illumination into a per-point latent representation, which a second network projects to the 2D image; presented as a learned extension of point-based global illumination and deferred shading.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Network weights trained across scenes for ambient occlusion, global illumination and subsurface scattering against path-traced references.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The weights; the network is re-evaluated on the edited point cloud.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not a target; effects shown are smooth (AO, diffuse GI, SSS).
entries.cost_claims: Claims most of the efficiency of 2D screen-space methods with better temporal coherence; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Smooth transport only; no linearity or physical constraints.
entries.relevance: Early proof that a transport response conditioned on 3D geometry transfers to unseen configurations without retraining — for low-frequency effects.

entries.work: Kallweit, Müller, McWilliams, Gross, Novák — Deep Scattering: Rendering Atmospheric Clouds with Radiance-Predicting Neural Networks
entries.mechanism: Low-order scattering is integrated by Monte Carlo; multiple scattering is predicted by a network fed a hierarchical 3D descriptor of the cloud density around the shading point, oriented with respect to the light, fed progressively into the network.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A network pre-trained on tens of cloud exemplars; no per-cloud precomputation.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The weights: the descriptor is re-sampled from the current density, so the prediction applies to unseen and animated clouds.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not applicable: high-order volumetric scattering is smooth; the sharp, low-order part is kept in Monte Carlo.
entries.cost_claims: Images nearly indistinguishable from the reference within seconds, interactively, versus very long path-traced convergence for high-albedo clouds.
entries.limitation: One material class (clouds), one distant light direction as conditioning; smooth transport.
entries.relevance: The cleanest precedent for the hybrid 'path-trace the first events exactly, predict the higher-order remainder from a geometry descriptor sampled around the query, no retraining for new geometry'. It works where the remainder is smooth and the descriptor is centred on the query point.

entries.work: Vicini, Koltun, Jakob — A Learned Shape-Adaptive Subsurface Scattering Model
entries.mechanism: A conditional autoencoder samples the exit location of subsurface light directly on the surface, conditioned on a low-order polynomial fit of the local geometry (capturing curvature, thickness, corners) and the medium parameters, replacing internal path tracing.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A network trained once across shapes and media; at render time only a local polynomial fit of the current geometry is computed.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The weights; the geometric conditioning is recomputed locally, so it applies to unseen shapes.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not applicable (diffusive subsurface transport); it is a sampling model with a pdf, used inside a path tracer.
entries.cost_claims: Retains the speed of analytic BSSRDF models with accuracy closer to volumetric path tracing.
entries.limitation: Local geometric descriptor; transport is smooth and short-range.
entries.relevance: A learned transport response conditioned on geometry that transfers without retraining AND remains an unbiased-style sampler inside path tracing, because it is formulated as a sampling distribution rather than a table of radiance.

entries.work: Zhu, Tang, Ma — DeepRTE: Pre-trained Attention-based Neural Network for Radiative Transfer
entries.mechanism: A mesh-free, attention-based neural operator for the steady-state radiative transfer equation whose architecture and training data follow Green's-function theory: it is pre-trained on delta-function inflow boundary conditions and is then applied 'zero-shot' to other inputs.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Operator network weights (boundary/source data -> solution), few parameters by the authors' account.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The abstract claims zero-shot capability but does not say whether it covers unseen geometries or coefficient fields; not established.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Not applicable: participating-media RTE in scientific-computing settings, not surface rendering with specular kernels.
entries.cost_claims: Claims higher efficiency than traditional solvers and other neural approaches; no numbers read.
entries.limitation: Outside graphics; small canonical domains; generalisation scope unclear. A separate neutron-transport operator-learning preprint found in the same search (arXiv 2602.15890) reports limited generalisation when the physical configuration changes.
entries.relevance: The nearest verified instance of explicit Green's-function operator learning for a transport equation: training on delta sources is the operator-learning analogue of source-independent supervision. I found no counterpart for the surface rendering equation.

entries.work: Li, Wiedemann, Mitchell — Deep Precomputed Radiance Transfer for Deformable Objects
entries.mechanism: A U-Net operating on geometry images (harmonic-map parameterisation) of the current shape predicts per-frame spherical-harmonic transfer coefficients, replacing Monte Carlo PRT precomputation for each deformation state.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A CNN trained on PRT data of one deformable object across its deformations.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The network is re-evaluated on the deformed shape and emits a new linear transfer operator; no retraining within the object's deformation family.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Excluded: SH transfer under low-frequency distant lighting for a single object.
entries.cost_claims: Real-time transfer prediction versus per-frame Monte Carlo projection; compared with a linear morphable-model baseline.
entries.limitation: One object family, low frequency, distant light, self-transfer only.
entries.relevance: A verified case of exactly the pattern 'a network sees current geometry and emits the coefficients of a linear, source-independent transfer operator', demonstrated only for band-limited self-transfer.

implications: In the surveyed literature, validity under rigid edits and sharp glossy interreflection do not occur together in any precomputed or learned operator. Operators that carry glossy indirect detail (Kontkanen 2006, RRF 2013, Raghavan 2023, neural-radiosity variants) are fixed-geometry and must be recomputed or retrained after an edit; operators that survive rigid edits (neighborhood transfer, shadow fields, radiance transfer fields, MRT, TransGI, NeLT as described) are low-frequency or diffuse between objects, or drop inter-object interreflection altogether (shadow fields: direct lighting only, by the authors' statement).

Rigid-edit validity in the classical line comes from one structural move: the operator is owned by an entity and stored in that entity's frame, and inter-entity transport is composed at run time. The composition step is where angular frequency is lost: fields are sampled on sparse shells, and a sender's response is indexed by a coarse summary of what reaches it. Shadow fields at all-frequency resolution already cost 0.1 fps and hundreds of MB for visibility alone.

Reduced (low-rank) operators reproduce only what their input prior spans. MRT states this as a limitation (lighting outside the prior cannot be captured; one mode acts as an 'intelligent ambient term') and names high-frequency glossy transport as an open problem. A low-rank global term that compensates without geometric specificity is the documented behaviour of this class.

All-frequency PRT obtained sharpness through sparse, nonlinear selection in a localized basis (Haar wavelets in Ng 2004, Liu 2004, Raghavan 2023), not through low rank. The sparsity pattern is a property of one configuration, which is why these operators are per-scene, and the best learned version still fails at mirror roughness 0.05 with 64 wavelets.

Learned GI systems that show sharp effects keep the sharp relation in explicit ray tracing and query the learned quantity only at rough vertices (Neural Radiosity traces specular chains to the first non-specular hit; Diolatzis et al. suggest tracing specular bounces in buffer generation; TransGI needs an extra per-pixel ray for specular). Querying a cached outgoing-radiance table through a narrow lobe is recognised as a failure mode, and the published responses (cone encoding, OctaOctree) are angular-resolution-adaptive storage at fixed geometry.

The one surveyed method that evaluates light -> glossy sender -> receiver transport robustly in dynamic scenes (Xu et al. 2014) does it by integrating over the sender with the sender lobe in closed form, i.e. sender-centred rather than receiver-gathered, and caches nothing; it is limited to one bounce.

Hierarchical-radiosity work (Drettakis and Sillion 1997) shows that the operator entries invalidated by a rigid move are geometrically identifiable (links whose shaft is cut) and can be updated selectively; this was shown for diffuse links only, and the number of affected entries grows with the operator's directional resolution.

Learned methods that tolerate edits do so in one of two ways: (a) the pose is an input coordinate of a per-scene model trained over a declared range (Diolatzis 2022: 5-18 h, quality drops as variables grow; Dynamic Neural Radiosity), which is interpolation, not transfer; or (b) a cross-scene network is re-evaluated on the new geometry (RenderFormer, Xu et al. 2025, Hermosilla 2019, LightFormer), which gives up linearity in the source and any passivity guarantee and is reported to be weak on higher-order specular chains, sharp indirect highlights and scale (RenderFormer: about three specular bounces, 4,096 training triangles, diffuse lights only; Xu et al.: glossy 'preliminary', missed intricate indirect highlights).

Hard structural constraints of the tested mechanism (source independence, linearity, non-negativity) exist in classical transfer matrices and partly in per-scene neural PRT (dot product with lighting coefficients in Raghavan 2023 and TransGI). Among cross-scene learned models I found none that enforces them; RenderFormer handles multiple or coloured lights by rendering separately and summing.

Geometry-descriptor-conditioned predictors that transfer without retraining and coexist with exact low-order path tracing exist for smooth transport (Deep Scattering for clouds, the shape-adaptive SSS model). In both, the predicted remainder is smooth and the descriptor is centred on the query; neither involves a narrow sender lobe far from the query.

Economic evidence is thin for the stated target. Classical PRT speed-ups are bought with hours of per-scene or per-object precompute and tens to hundreds of MB. Cross-scene networks report 28-183x versus Cycles at 4,096 spp (RenderFormer, small scenes, not equal quality) or sub-second frames versus 64 spp while stating they are not a drop-in replacement (Xu et al. 2025). No surveyed work reports a matched-quality cost advantage over path tracing for sharp glossy interreflection after a geometry edit.

I found no verified work applying neural-operator / Green's-function learning (DeepONet, FNO or similar) or learned preconditioners to the surface rendering equation. The nearest verified items are DeepRTE (Green's-function-motivated operator for the RTE in media), neural radiosity (residual minimisation with self-training, per scene) and generic learned preconditioners for sparse PDE systems; the operator-learning literature found alongside reports weak extrapolation when the physical configuration changes.
closest_precedents: Li, Wiedemann, Mitchell 2019 (DeepPRT): a network reads the current geometry and emits coefficients of a linear, source-independent transfer operator without retraining — demonstrated only for low-frequency SH self-transfer of one deformable object under distant light.

Loos et al. 2011 (Modular Radiance Transfer): source-independent reduced direct-to-indirect operators per shape, coupled through reduced interface lightfields and re-assembled under re-arrangement — diffuse, low-rank prior, glossy explicitly left open.

Pan et al. 2007 (radiance transfer fields) on top of Zhou et al. 2005 (shadow fields): per-object linear operator from incident light on the object to the radiance field around it, valid under arbitrary rigid motion and composed at run time — low-frequency lighting only; shadow fields themselves are direct-only.

Xu et al. 2025 (Generalizable Light Transport 3D Embedding): cross-scene transformer that encodes geometry/material/emitter point clouds into a transport embedding reused on unseen and edited scenes — not linear in the source, no visibility rays, diffuse-first with preliminary glossy.

Zeng et al. 2025 (RenderFormer, and RenderFormer++ 2026 by abstract): view-independent triangle-to-triangle transport stage that transfers to unseen configurations without retraining — source enters as emissive tokens (not source-independent), about three specular bounces, small scenes.

Deng et al. 2025 (TransGI) and Zheng et al. 2023 (NeLT): object-owned learned transfer that travels with rigid objects, inter-object light supplied by a per-frame lighting state — SH-band-limited (TransGI, read) / fidelity unverified (NeLT, abstract only).

Kallweit et al. 2017 (Deep Scattering): path-trace low orders exactly and predict the higher-order remainder from a geometry descriptor sampled at render time, no retraining for new geometry — smooth volumetric transport, descriptor centred on the query point.

Hašan et al. 2006 / Kontkanen et al. 2006 / Lehtinen et al. 2008: the explicit direct-to-indirect and global transport operators (wavelet, 4D wavelet with glossy, meshless hierarchical) that a geometry-conditioned generator would have to reproduce — all precomputed for one fixed scene.

Raghavan et al. 2023: learned, linear-in-lighting, wavelet-basis indirect transport with glossy reflections and caustics — per scene, static geometry, about 16 h training, degrades at near-mirror roughness.

Zhu, Tang, Ma 2025 (DeepRTE): operator network trained on delta-function inflow (Green's-function supervision) for the radiative transfer equation — the nearest verified operator-learning analogue of source-independent supervision, outside surface rendering.
unverified_or_uncertain: NeLT (Zheng et al., ACM TOG 2023, DOI 10.1145/3596491): existence, authors and abstract confirmed; the mechanism details (lighting encoding, how per-object functions are composed, whether inter-object glossy transport is represented, performance) come from secondary summaries only — the paper text was not accessible.

Pan et al. 2007 (radiance transfer fields): the Eurographics digital library was unreachable for direct fetch; abstract content is from a search-result summary. Author list is reported inconsistently across records (Pan, Wang, Liu, Peng, Bao per the EG metadata). The statement that incident light on the sender is summarised coarsely is my recollection.

Iwasaki, Dobashi, Yoshimoto, Nishita 2007 (EGSR, PRT for dynamic scenes with interreflection) and Mei, Shi, Wu 2004 (Spherical Radiance Transport Maps, CGF 23(3)): existence confirmed by library records; mechanisms known to me only at abstract/snippet level and folded into the Pan et al. entry.

Works confirmed to exist in search results but not read, and therefore not given entries: Wang, Tran, Luebke 2004 (separable BRDF all-frequency relighting); Green, Kautz, Matusik, Durand 2006 (non-linear Gaussian view-dependent transport, rigid objects, distant light); Sloan, Luna, Snyder 2005 (local deformable PRT with zonal harmonics); Ren et al. 2006 (SH exponentiation soft shadows); Dachsbacher et al. 2007 (implicit visibility and antiradiance — I could not confirm from the abstract whether glossy transport is handled; a related paper notes dynamic objects are restricted by tessellation needs); Müller et al. 2021 (real-time neural radiance caching, online training with no pretraining 'since generalizing a pretrained network to new dynamic scenes is hard'); Xu, Zeng, Wu, Wang, Yan 2022 (lightweight neural basis functions with learned product/rotation operators — the 10-40x figure came from a truncated snippet); Coomans et al. 2024 (real-time neural rendering of dynamic light fields — rigid-object handling not confirmed); Gao et al. 2022 (Neural Global Illumination under dynamic area lights, TVCG — PDF too large to fetch); Gai, Wang, Li 2025 (arXiv 2508.08826, screen-space diffuse indirect, claims unseen-scene generalisation).

Zheng et al. 2024, 'Neural Global Illumination via Superposed Deformable Feature Fields' (SIGGRAPH Asia 2024): seen only as a citation inside another paper's reference list; not independently verified or read.

Details stated from memory rather than from a source read in this session: that PRT neighborhood transfer has no feedback from receiver to sender; that Ng et al. 2004 is restricted to static geometry; that gather samples in Hašan et al. 2006 are diffuse senders; that Lehtinen et al. 2008 is primarily diffuse and static; that Xu et al. 2014 needs no scene precomputation and approximates indirect visibility; whether Liu et al. 2004 includes interreflection in its transfer.

Dynamic Neural Radiosity (Su et al. 2024): only the project-page abstract was read (the PDF exceeded the fetch limit); the supported variable types, out-of-range behaviour, glossy handling and cost numbers are not verified.

Neural Cone Radiosity (arXiv 2509.07522) and OctaOctree Neural Radiosity (arXiv 2606.08469), RenderFormer++ (arXiv 2606.30380), DeepRTE (arXiv 2505.23190): arXiv abstracts only; all are preprints as far as I could see. A search snippet attributed the phrase 'pre-filtered neural operators' to the cone-radiosity paper; the abstract itself speaks of a pre-filtered multi-resolution hash grid.
RenderFormer training-set size and schedule: the extracted HTML appeared to duplicate digits; the figures given (order of millions of scenes, about 8 days on 8 A100s) are approximate.

TransGI is an arXiv preprint with no peer-reviewed venue listed; the '75 values = 25 SH coefficients x 3 channels' reading is an interpretation, and rotation under rigid motion was not separately evaluated in the paper.

RRF (Ren et al. 2013): I read only the abstract page; that geometry is fixed and only the local light and view vary is consistent with the abstract but the treatment of moving objects was not checked in the paper.

Negative search results are not proof of absence: I found no paper applying DeepONet/FNO-style neural operators, learned Green's functions or learned preconditioners specifically to the surface rendering equation, and no 'neural shadow fields' style work, in a limited number of queries. Foundational operator formalisms (Arvo 1995; Veach 1997) and static-geometry probe methods (e.g. Kristensen et al. 2005; Silvennoinen and Lehtinen 2017) were not searched or verified in this session.

angle: Theory and practice of sharp / specular light transport and of principled partitions of transport: Heckbert path classes and multi-pass diffuse/specular splits, why gathering fails and shooting / bidirectional / manifold methods succeed for caustics, adjoint (importance) refinement, hierarchical / wavelet / clustering radiosity and its glossy extensions, discontinuity meshing, incremental and line-space dynamic radiosity, implicit visibility (antiradiance), the operator view (Arvo, Veach, compactness), low-rank / hierarchical-matrix compression and what bounds rank, and frequency / bandwidth results on the sampling density needed for glossy lobes.

entries.work: Heckbert, 'Adaptive Radiosity Textures for Bidirectional Ray Tracing'
entries.mechanism: Splits each surface interaction into diffuse plus specular; the specular part is computed on the fly as in ray tracing, the diffuse part (radiosity) is stored in adaptive per-surface textures ('rexes') filled by a light pass that shoots photons from lights and bright surfaces, then read by an eye pass. The regular-expression path notation L(S|D)*E used to classify which paths each pass owns is attributed to Heckbert (Veach's thesis section 8.3.1 reviews it as 'Heckbert's regular expression notation').
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: View-independent radiosity textures on diffuse surfaces (the L(S|D)*D prefix), adaptively subdivided to the resolution the image needs; a 'size pass' decides that resolution.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing is designed for edits: the textures hold source- and geometry-specific radiosity, so any edit that changes visibility or the light paths requires re-shooting the affected light paths.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Caustics (LS+D) are deposited by shooting from the light, never gathered; specular chains toward the eye (DS*E) are traced from the eye. Glossy (neither D nor S) has no natural owner in the notation.
entries.cost_claims: None quantitative in the abstract.
entries.limitation: The exclusive split relies on a binary D/S material model; the stored quantity is radiosity, not a transport operator, so it is source-dependent.
entries.relevance: Origin of the path-class bookkeeping that makes a partition provably exclusive: a path belongs to exactly one class by the D/S types of its vertices, and the light -> sharp reflector -> diffuse family is assigned to a light-driven (shooting) pass by construction.

entries.work: Wallace, Cohen, Greenberg, 'A Two-Pass Solution to the Rendering Equation' and Sillion & Puech, 'A General Two-Pass Method Integrating Specular and Diffuse Reflection'
entries.mechanism: Pass 1 is a view-independent radiosity solve extended so that diffuse-to-diffuse transfer includes paths that pass via specular reflection/transmission (Sillion & Puech: 'extended form factors', computed by ray-traced adaptive sampling for arbitrary geometry and refraction); pass 2 is view-dependent and adds the specular chain toward the eye. Sillion & Puech analyse the approaches by 'introducing the corresponding reflection operators'.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A geometry-dependent, source-independent matrix of (extended) form factors between diffuse patches; then a source-dependent radiosity solution.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: The form-factor matrix is purely geometric, so entries whose patch pair and intervening specular chain are untouched by an edit remain valid; entries whose visibility or specular chain changed must be recomputed (the papers do not address edits).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Ideal specular only. The D S* D transfer is folded into the operator by tracing through the mirrors from the diffuse sender/receiver, i.e. the specular chain is resolved geometrically per patch pair rather than by angular binning. No glossy lobes.
entries.cost_claims: None quantitative in the abstracts; extended form factors cost a ray tree per form-factor sample.
entries.limitation: Spatial resolution of the caustic is the patch mesh; restricted to diffuse + ideal specular; limited specular depth in the 1987 version (planar mirrors, recalled from memory).
entries.relevance: Earliest precedent for a geometry-only linear operator that already contains sharp specular interreflection: the split 'D-to-D including S* (stored) / S*E (view pass)' is physically exclusive, and the sharp relation is carried by exact ray geometry inside the operator entry, not by a directional basis.

entries.work: Immel, Cohen, Greenberg, 'A Radiosity Method for Non-Diffuse Environments' and Sillion, Arvo, Westin, Greenberg, 'A Global Illumination Solution for General Reflectance Distributions'
entries.mechanism: Finite-element radiance: Immel et al. discretise surfaces and the hemisphere of directions and solve for 'the light leaving each surface in each direction' (viewer-independent); Sillion et al. replace direction bins by spherical-harmonic coefficients for both BRDFs and per-patch outgoing intensity distributions, inside a two-pass ray-casting radiosity framework.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A patch x direction (bins or SH) representation of outgoing radiance and the corresponding patch-direction to patch-direction transfer coefficients.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not addressed. Transfer coefficients are geometric and in principle reusable where unaffected; the solved directional radiance is source- and geometry-specific.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Immel et al. demonstrate 'secondary light sources' such as a spotlight reflected by a mirror onto a wall, but only at the resolution of the direction discretisation; Sillion et al. explicitly keep ideal specular out of the SH representation and handle it by a separate ray-traced pass (recalled from memory beyond the abstract).
entries.cost_claims: None in the abstracts; the method of Immel et al. is widely described (e.g. by Christensen et al. 1997) as tractable only for very small environments.
entries.limitation: Storage and solve cost scale with patches x directions; a fixed angular basis blurs or aliases narrow lobes; SH ringing for sharp lobes.
entries.relevance: This is the same data structure as a (surface patch x direction bin) table driven by a linear operator. The historical outcome was that fixed directional discretisations were kept for broad lobes and sharp lobes were moved to a ray-traced pass.

entries.work: Aupperle & Hanrahan, 'A Hierarchical Illumination Algorithm for Surfaces with Glossy Reflection'
entries.mechanism: Reformulates glossy transport as discrete three-point transport (source element -> reflector element -> receiver element) with a new reflectance measure, 'area reflectance', which yields an error estimate over triples of elements and hence hierarchical refinement.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A hierarchy of element-triple interactions refined to an error bound; radiance is stored per element pair (i.e. direction is represented by 'toward which other element').
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not addressed. Triple links are geometric, so they are reusable only if none of the three elements nor their mutual visibility changed.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Glossy lobes are resolved by refining the triples until the area reflectance is well approximated; a sharper lobe forces deeper refinement of all three elements.
entries.cost_claims: O(n log n) interactions for sufficient refinement (nearly linear in trials) versus O(n^3) element triples for a naive implementation.
entries.limitation: Refinement depth, and so the constant, grows as lobes narrow; ideal mirrors are outside the finite-element formulation.
entries.relevance: Shows an alternative directional parameterisation: direction encoded by sender-receiver element pairs (two-point radiance) instead of fixed angular bins, so angular resolution adapts to geometry and BRDF automatically - at the price of the link structure depending on scene geometry.

entries.work: Christensen, Stollnitz, Salesin, DeRose, 'Global Illumination of Glossy Environments Using Wavelets and Importance' and Christensen, Lischinski, Stollnitz, Salesin, 'Clustering for Glossy Global Illumination'
entries.mechanism: Radiance and importance are represented in a four-dimensional (2 spatial + 2 angular) Haar wavelet basis per patch, the transport operator is wavelet-decomposed (transport coefficients are six-dimensional integrals), refinement is importance-driven, and a final gather renders the image. The 1997 paper treats clusters as points carrying directional distributions of radiance and importance, with error bounds for cluster-to-cluster transfers.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Sparse adaptive 4D wavelet coefficients of radiance / importance and the sparse set of transport links actually needed for the view.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not addressed; link structure and refinement are specific to the geometry, lighting and (through importance) the view.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Glossy reflection is handled by adaptive refinement of angular wavelets where radiance x importance is large. The 1997 paper calls the 1996 method 'the wavelet version of Immel's algorithm' and notes these methods are 'the most efficient to date ... in small glossy environments'.
entries.cost_claims: 1996 method needs O(p^2) initial interactions for p surfaces; clustering gives O(p) links / O(p) solve for fixed directional resolution, with O(p log p) hierarchy construction.
entries.limitation: Per-cluster storage is proportional to the number of directional basis functions; complexity claims hold 'for a fixed directional resolution', i.e. they do not cover the growth needed for sharp lobes. A final gather is required to hide finite-element artefacts.
entries.relevance: The most developed attempt at a hierarchical spatial-angular basis for glossy interreflection. Its affordability came from adaptivity driven by the specific light and view (importance), which a source-independent and view-independent operator does not have.

entries.work: Chen, Rushmeier, Miller, Turner, 'A Progressive Multi-Pass Method for Global Illumination'
entries.mechanism: Combines progressive-refinement radiosity, Monte Carlo path tracing and light ray tracing, organised as a radiosity pass, a high-frequency refinement pass and a low-frequency refinement pass, with 'light source reclassification' and 'caustics reconstruction'.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: A coarse radiosity solution used as a preprocess for path tracing, plus caustic maps reconstructed from light rays.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not addressed.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: High-frequency transport (caustics) is taken out of the radiosity solution and computed by light ray tracing; care is needed so each path class is counted once (source reclassification).
entries.cost_claims: None quantitative in the abstract; progressive display of 'most useful information ... as early as possible'.
entries.limitation: Partition is by frequency class chosen per source and material type; glossy middle ground is handled by path tracing.
entries.relevance: A worked example of a partition by frequency content (low-frequency stored / high-frequency traced from the light / remainder path traced) with explicit bookkeeping to keep the classes exclusive.

entries.work: Jensen, 'Global Illumination using Photon Maps'
entries.mechanism: Two-pass: photons are emitted from lights, traced, and stored at every non-specular hit in a geometry-independent kd-tree; a high-resolution caustics photon map is visualised directly, a low-resolution global map is read after a final-gather bounce and also guides sampling.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Source-dependent flux samples (photon maps), decoupled from surface tessellation.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing by design; photons whose paths intersect the changed geometry are invalid (later selective photon tracing work re-shoots only those; see unverified list).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Caustic paths are found by shooting from the light, which samples the reflector's lobe exactly; density estimation then trades variance for spatial blur. The abstract motivates the method by radiosity becoming 'prohibitive' with glossy reflections.
entries.cost_claims: None quantitative in the abstract; compared against the Radiance program.
entries.limitation: Stores radiance for one lighting state; density-estimation bias (blur) on the caustic; on glossy receivers needs many photons or path continuation.
entries.relevance: The standard demonstration that the light -> specular -> diffuse family is cheap from the light side and expensive from the receiver side, and that the practical partition is 'caustic part read directly, smooth part read through a diffuse gather'.

entries.work: Veach, 'Robust Monte Carlo Methods for Light Transport Simulation' (PhD thesis), esp. chapters 4, 7, 8.3
entries.mechanism: Linear-operator formulation of transport (scattering and propagation operators, measurement, importance transport by adjoint operators), a self-adjoint formulation for physically valid scenes, and the path-integral formulation. Section 8.3 extends Heckbert's notation to full paths and proves Theorem 8.3: a path can be generated by local sampling iff it contains the substring DD; otherwise 'there are not enough D vertices'. Section 8.3.4 proposes 'connectors' that generate specular chains between two D vertices.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Nothing; this is theory plus unbiased estimators (BDPT with multiple importance sampling, Metropolis).
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not applicable (no stored state).
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: A specular vertex forces one neighbour to be generated by sampling its BSDF (Lemma 8.1). For near-specular configurations the paths are not missing but 'will be sampled with high variance'. Bidirectional sampling succeeds for LS+DE because the specular vertex is sampled from the light side and the DD edge is the connection.
entries.cost_claims: None for this section.
entries.limitation: The theorem is for ideal S; for narrow glossy lobes it becomes a variance statement, not an impossibility.
entries.relevance: Gives the exact criterion for which path families a receiver-side gather can and cannot resolve, and the vocabulary (chain separators, connectors) for partitions that are exclusive. A fixed set of receiver rays that must land inside a sender's narrow lobe is the high-variance limit of the missing-DD case.

entries.work: Kaplanyan & Dachsbacher, 'Path Space Regularization for Holistic and Robust Light Transport'
entries.mechanism: Identifies paths that cannot be sampled without bias (Veach's criterion) and selectively mollifies individual S interactions into D (angular delta replaced by a finite-support kernel of angle alpha = arctan(r/l)), with a bandwidth that shrinks to zero under derived consistency conditions.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Nothing; an estimator modification.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Not applicable.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Sharp lobes are widened just enough to be connectable, only on paths that need it; bias vanishes only as the mollification bandwidth goes to zero. Notes photon mapping relaxes the DD condition by merging light and camera sub-paths.
entries.cost_claims: Equal-time comparisons (e.g. 2 h) showing effects missing from PT / MLT / PPM; no asymptotic cost claim beyond convergence-rate conditions.
entries.limitation: Biased at any finite bandwidth; convergence slower than unbiased sampling where the latter exists.
entries.relevance: Formalises what a finite angular bin does to a sharp lobe: it is a mollifier of fixed, non-vanishing bandwidth, so its error is a blur of that width and does not decrease with more samples.

entries.work: Mitchell & Hanrahan, 'Illumination from Curved Reflectors'
entries.mechanism: Computes illumination reflected from curved mirrors onto other surfaces by finding extremal (Fermat) paths from the light to the receiver via the mirrors with interval analysis, then computing irradiance from the Gaussian curvature of the geometric wavefront.
entries.what_is_precomputed_or_learned: Nothing stored; per-receiver-point root finding.
entries.what_stays_valid_under_geometry_edits: Nothing stored; but the formulation is purely geometric, so after a rigid edit the same solver applies unchanged. Chen & Arvo (TOG 2000, 'Theory and Application of Specular Path Perturbation', known here only from abstract-level descriptions) expand a known specular path in a Taylor series to update it under small changes.
entries.handling_of_sharp_glossy_interreflection: Exact for ideal mirrors: the light -> mirror -> receiver relation is a discrete set of deterministic paths with a closed-form intensity (wavefront curvature), not an integral that needs angular sampling.
entries.cost_claims: None in the abstract.
entries.limitation: Ideal specular, implicit/analytic surfaces; interval Newton cost; multiple bounces compound.
entries.relevance: Establishes that the sharp sender -> receiver relation is determined by geometry alone (source position, reflector shape, receiver point) and is finite-dimensional per endpoint pair - the information a binned linear operator has to approximate by resolution.

entries.work: Jakob & Marschner, 'Manifold Exploration: A Markov Chain Monte Carlo Technique for Rendering Scenes with Difficult Specular Transport'
